title: Waddy Young: Oklahoma's First Consensus All-American
question: Who was the first consensus All-American in Oklahoma football history?
answer: End Waddy Young, who played at Oklahoma from 1936 to 1938, was the Sooners' first consensus All-American, earning the honor in 1938. He entered the College Football Hall of Fame in 1986.
summary: Waddy Young, a Ponca City end, became Oklahoma's first consensus All-American in 1938, reached the College Football Hall of Fame, and died a war hero in 1945.
body: Walter Roland "Waddy" Young grew up in Ponca City, Oklahoma, where he was an All-State end in high school. He played end for the Sooners from 1936 through 1938, a 6-foot-2 lineman of about 200 pounds who was named All-Conference in 1937 and 1938.

His senior season of 1938 made history. Young was a consensus All-American, selected by the Associated Press, Collier's and the International News Service, which made him the first Oklahoma player to earn that distinction. He was also a heavyweight wrestler for OU.

The team around him broke ground too. Under coach Tom Stidham, the 1938 Sooners won the program's first Big Six championship and earned its first bowl invitation, to the 1939 Orange Bowl. Young was a central figure on that squad.
The Brooklyn Dodgers of the NFL selected him in the third round of the 1939 draft, and he played two seasons in Brooklyn before joining the Army Air Corps.

Young became a B-29 pilot and a captain. On January 9, 1945, after a raid on Tokyo, he turned back to help a badly damaged bomber, and the two planes collided; he was killed. He was awarded the Distinguished Flying Cross, and the College Football Hall of Fame inducted him in 1986.
